record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
record.original_question: For a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length completely reducible if and only if, for every positive integer n, the n-th cohomology of the meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any bimodule vanishes? Equivalently, for a grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is complete reducibility of every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length equivalent to vanishing of the n-th cohomology for every positive integer n and every bimodule?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. Every grading-restricted generalized module of ﬁnite length for a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if forn∈ Z+, the n-th cohomology of the meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coeﬃcients in any bimodule is 0. In particular, every grading-restricted generalized module of ﬁnite length for a grading-restricted vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if for n ∈ Z+, the n-th cohomology of the grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coeﬃcients in any bimodule (whose left and right actions can be diﬀerent) is 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} V_{(n)}$ be a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra (a $\mathbb{Z}$-graded vector space equipped with a vertex map $Y_V\colon V\otimes V\to V[[x,x^{-1}]]$, vacuum $\mathbf{1}$, and a grading operator, satisfying the rationality, identity, and associativity axioms appropriate to non-commutative vertex algebras, where $Y_V(u,x)v$ involves possibly non-symmetric operator products), with the standard notion of bimodule (a graded vector space with compatible left and right vertex operator actions, whose left and right actions need not coincide) and with the cohomology $H^n(V,W)$ ($n\in\mathbb{Z}_+$) defined as the cohomology of the cochain complex of linear maps $V^{\otimes n}\to \widetilde{W}$ satisfying the appropriate composability and $D$-derivative properties, with coboundary given by the standard vertex algebra cochain differential.

A grading-restricted generalized $V$-module is a graded module on which the grading operator acts with finite-dimensional generalized eigenspaces bounded below in real part. Such a module has finite length if it admits a finite composition series of irreducible grading-restricted generalized submodules. The module is completely reducible if every grading-restricted generalized submodule has a complement.

Decide whether the following equivalence holds:

Every grading-restricted generalized $V$-module of finite length is completely reducible if and only if, for every positive integer $n$ and every $V$-bimodule $W$, $H^n(V,W)=0$.

In particular, settle the corresponding equivalence in the special case where $V$ is a grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, with cohomology computed using bimodules whose left and right actions may differ.
artifact.status_search_result: Huang and Qi have established one direction under a convergence assumption: vanishing of the first cohomology with coefficients in every bimodule implies that left modules of finite length satisfying a composability condition are completely reducible. The full equivalence (for all $n$ and the converse) appears not to have been resolved; subsequent work studies the first cohomology, derivations, and extensions, but the conjecture in its full form remains open.

status_evidence.title: The first cohomology, derivations and the reductivity of a (meromorphic open-string) vertex algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Gives a criterion for complete reducibility of modules using the first cohomology of a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra; under conditions on H^1 with coefficients in every bimodule, left modules of finite length satisfying composability are completely reducible.
status_evidence.claim: One direction of the conjecture (vanishing of first cohomology implies complete reducibility) has been established under additional assumptions, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: On the extensions of the left modules for a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, I
status_evidence.snippet: Continues the study of cohomology and extensions for meromorphic open-string vertex algebras, building on the program initiated to address the reductivity-cohomology conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains an active topic with ongoing partial results rather than a complete proof.
